_comment: SHIPPED BENCH for the eth-chiplet pad-ring netlist. THE REAL FLASH BOOTS IT.
WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY THIS FILE IS THE ONE THE GATE GRADES
Until 2026-08-19 this spec carried a `forces` entry that HELD
chip_core_remap_ctrl[2] high, and said so in its own reason field: 'This
bench models no flash device, so CPU1 never reaches that write and CPU0
never fetches at all.' It proved CPU0's ROM FETCH PATH and nothing about
the CPU1->CPU0 handshake. There is now a flash device on the QSPI pins, so
the force is DELETED rather than explained, and CPU0 leaves reset here only
because CPU1's stage-0 walked its whole boot - attempt counter, XiP
bring-up, mailbox publish, boot table, image copy, CRC - and wrote 0x4
itself.
The forced variant still exists, at bench/eth_chiplet_fp1505_forced.json.
It is a DIAGNOSTIC FALLBACK, it is NOT in GLSN_ITEMS, and the gate never
grades it. See ../Makefile, section THE FALLBACK.
THE DEVICE IS NOT DECLARED IN THIS FILE, because this schema cannot
instantiate a module. It is bound in from ../flash/gls_flash_attach.sv,
which ../Makefile adds to the compile alongside the vendor SST26VF064B
model. What this spec contributes is the two NETS that binding needs:
QSPI_IO already had pullups, and QSPI_SCLK and QSPI_nCS are added to `tiez`
so the generator declares them and wires them to the DUT. Without those two
entries the DUT's QSPI clock and chip-select are left UNCONNECTED and the
bound flash sees a floating clock.
IMAGE PROVENANCE TRAVELS WITH THE VERDICT. The boot image is BENCH-SUPPLIED:
a run that reached the application only because the testbench handed the
design a valid image is not the design booting unaided. inputs.txt records
flash_image.hex with its sha256 under `staged bench inputs`, and sim.log
carries the attachment's own GLSN-FLASH banner. Both are published evidence.
Quote neither result without them.
THE BOOTGATE IS NOT A SUCCESS CRITERION AND THERE IS NO `expects` ON IT.
stage0_bootrom_chip_core/main.c writes NETWORK_CORE_BOOTGATE (0x4) TWICE:
main.c:383  on the success path, immediately before jumping to IMEM
main.c:403  UNCONDITIONALLY, after every candidate INCLUDING the golden
recovery image has failed, immediately before halt()
The second write is deliberate and its own comment says why - 'otherwise a
blank flash silently holds CPU0 in reset and the debug UART never transmits
(the cpu0_bootgate silent-UART bug)'. So a BLANK, ABSENT, CORRUPT or
WRONG-CRC flash STILL releases CPU0, and CPU0 still fetches its MSP and
reset vector out of eth_rom. At the bootgate, and at the eth_rom port, that
is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real boot. A gate built on either would report
PASS on an image that never parsed. `make -C ASIC/gls-netlist
negative-control` runs exactly that case and requires this spec to go red.
WHAT SEPARATES THEM: cpu1_imem_write and cpu1_imem_fetch.
cpu1_imem_write  CPU1's copy_image -> NANOSOC_IMEM_BASE happens only after
a boot table validated and its MASTER entry passed
boot_entry_image, so writes landing in CPU1's IMEM macro
cannot be produced by a blank flash. Sound because
+define+INITIALIZE_MEMORY zero-fills this array at t=0:
anything non-zero in it was written by the design.
cpu1_imem_fetch  CPU1 EXECUTING out of that image. main.c:388 flips its own
REMAP and jumps only after nanosoc_crc32 over the copied
image matched the table's CRC, so this rung closes the gap
cpu1_imem_write alone leaves open - a copy whose CRC then
failed, since the copy happens before the check.
There is NO CPU1-side pre-stage of eth's IMEM, whatever a draft may say:
main.c:369-375 states the eth-IMEM admin window aliases CPU1's OWN IMEM at
0x10000000, so a pre-stage would overwrite the just-CRC'd MASTER image. Any
write to the eth IMEM macro is CPU0's own copy, after release.
THE 900x TIMING GAP IS A FREE DISCRIMINATOR, and cpu0_rom_idle_at_1ms spends
it. Forced, CPU0's first eth_rom fetch landed at 3.47 us. Booted for real it
lands in the MILLISECONDS, because CPU1 must first shift some 2.2 KB out of a
serial device. So 'at 1 ms the eth_rom had not been touched once' is true of
every real boot and impossible under any bench that releases CPU0 early -
which is to say, it fails the instant somebody reintroduces a force.
IT IS NOT A BLANK-FLASH RUNG, and the margin is smaller than it looks.
MEASURED 2026-08-19 by `make negative-control`: on an erased image CPU1's ROM
gives up and takes the main.c:403 release at 1.0215 ms, so cpu0_rom_idle_at_1ms
fires 21 us before that and PASSES the blank-flash run too. That is the right
outcome - it is a FORCE detector, with 285x margin against the 3.47 us a force
produces and 3.4x against a real boot's 3.4578 ms - but do not read it as
evidence about the image. cpu1_imem_write and cpu1_imem_fetch do that job.
THE ONE COUPLING IN THIS FILE. That assertion reads acc_eth_rom_port, the
access counter gen_netlist_tb.py emits for the eth_rom_port romwatch above
(`integer acc_<name> = 0;`). It is the only expression here that names a
GENERATOR identifier rather than a DESIGN one. If the generator renames it
the bench fails to COMPILE, loudly, at the line that says so - which is the
failure mode to prefer over a design signal that silently reads z.
NO `expects` ON chip_core_remap_ctrl_w, AND THE TRACE IS NARROWED TO BIT 2.
The net is `wire [3:0]` and only bit 2 has a driver (one flop, .Q at
nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads_pnr_pgc.v:533611); bits 0, 1 and 3 are undriven and
read z, so a 4-bit %0h trace printed `0xZ` on every run this bench has ever
done and told nobody anything. Bit 2 alone is observable, and it is traced -
as OBSERVATION, never as a verdict, for the two-writes reason above.
WHERE THIS GATE STOPS, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CHOICE.
It grades CPU1's boot end to end and CPU0 up to and including the branch to
its reset vector. It does NOT grade CPU0's own image copy or CPU0's CRC, and
the reason is that they DO NOT HAPPEN - not slowly, at all. Measured on the
fp1505 routed netlist 2026-08-19 with this exact device and image, over
600,000 cycles (12 ms, 2.4x the shipped window):
eth_rom_port.accessed   PASS accesses=131611 xdata=0
eth_imem_write.accessed FAIL accesses=0
eth_sysctrl_remap_set   FAIL never
GLSN-TRACE: 10000 eth_imem_CEN = 0x1        (and never changes again)
CPU0 leaves reset at 3.4576 ms, reads its MSP and reset vector, branches to
the vector target, and then fetches 131,611 further words out of eth_rom over
the next 8.5 ms - a steady 0.31 fetches per cycle, so it is RUNNING - while
its IMEM macro's chip-enable never once falls. Whatever eth's stage-0 is doing
after the branch, it is not reaching copy_image. That is an open question for
the firmware/eth side and it is NOT something this bench should convert into
a permanent red: an assertion nobody can turn green stops being read.
So the two CPU0-side rungs were WRITTEN, RUN, MEASURED AND THEN REMOVED, and
this paragraph is here so that removal cannot later be mistaken for an
oversight or for a gate that stopped asking. eth_imem_CEN is still TRACED, so
the day CPU0 does reach its copy the transcript shows it and the rungs can be
restored from here. Until then:
A PASS ON THIS BENCH MEANS: both mask ROMs hold their firmware; CPU1 booted
a flash image end to end and is executing it; CPU0 was released BY CPU1 and
reached its own ROM. It does NOT mean CPU0 booted its application.
run_cycles = 250,000 (5 ms at the 20 ns reference clock). Measured here
2026-08-19: this netlist simulates about 4,450 reference cycles per CPU
second, so 250,000 cycles is about 60 s of run against 83 s of compile. The
4,000,000 an earlier draft carried would be 900 s for no extra rung: CPU0's
first eth_rom fetch lands at 3.4578 ms (MEASURED, 2026-08-19; the ~3.2 ms
figure in circulation is a projection) and everything this spec grades has
happened by then.
Inherited from the forced bench, and still true:
PROBES ARE AT THE MACROS' OWN PORT PINS, not on the AHB bus upstream. A
bus-level probe can be satisfied by the testbench itself, and the question is
specifically whether a CPU reaches the macro. CEN/A/Q at the macro boundary
cannot be produced by anything but the design.
The bidirectional pins carry WEAK PULLS rather than being left floating.
A floating inout is Z, which is X at the first gate downstream; the design's
own pad driver still wins whenever it drives, so this models a board pull-up
and not a tie-off. QSPI_IO keeps its pullups WITH the flash attached: in SPI
mode IO2/IO3 are the device's WP#/HOLD# inputs and nothing drives them.
_flash_nets_note: QSPI_SCLK (output) and QSPI_nCS (output) are real ports of
nanosoc_eth_chiplet_pads - verified in the netlist. They are declared here as
bare wires so ../flash/gls_flash_attach.sv can `bind` the SST26VF064B model
onto them. QSPI_IO[3:0] (inout) stays in `pullup`: the flash and the chip's
pads both tri-state it, and in SPI mode IO2/IO3 are the device's WP#/HOLD#
inputs that nothing drives at all.
